headline: Kai, the largest IPO in history couldn't turn the tape — the S&P logged a sixth straight loss, Taiwan capped its worst week since 1991, and the AI unwind is now global.
subline: S&P futures are off 0.6% after Thursday's 2% drop, a quarter-point December hike stays priced ahead of Wednesday's PCE, and bitcoin is holding four-month lows near $62,000.
asof: Pre-market · index values are futures · ≈6:40 AM ET Fri · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Sixth straight loss; Dow back below 50,000
items.sentence: The S&P 500 fell 2.0% Thursday to about 7,176 — a sixth straight decline and its longest losing streak since 2024, with the Dow closing back under 50,000 — in what Tickmill's morning outlook describes as a shift from orderly correction to broad liquidation.

items.title: Taiwan caps worst week since 1991 as Asia sells
items.sentence: Taiwan's market fell 6.2% Friday to cap its worst week since 1991, South Korea's Kospi closed down 5.2% and Japan's Nikkei dropped 5.1% as the AI chip selloff swept the region, per 24/7 Wall St.

items.title: Claims miss keeps a December hike priced
items.sentence: Markets still price a quarter-point Fed hike for December after weekly jobless claims rose to 203,000 against 197,000 expected, with October PCE due Wednesday as the next test, per Coin Gabbar.

items.title: 10-year eases to 5.05% as dollar nears 104
items.sentence: The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.05% — a fourth straight session of declines that still leaves it above 5% — while the dollar index pushed toward 104, per Yahoo Finance's Thursday morning brief.

items.title: Gold breaks toward $3,550; Brent holds $92.50
items.sentence: Spot gold slid toward $3,550 an ounce, one of its worst weeks in months as the dollar surged, while Brent held near $92.50 a barrel after fresh tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, per Tickmill.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin close Shenzhen with four-point plan
items.sentence: The first-ever Trump–Xi–Putin summit ended in Shenzhen with a four-point plan spanning nuclear risk, oil refining, UN reform and limits on the ICC's jurisdiction, per Havana Times' international briefs.

items.title: US and Venezuela sign deal restoring military ties
items.sentence: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed an agreement in Caracas restoring US–Venezuela military ties, covering joint training, intelligence sharing and border security, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.sentence: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar's security forces committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017 — the first such ruling against a state under the 1948 Genocide Convention, per Havana Times.

items.title: Israeli forces push past Gaza's Yellow Line
items.sentence: Israeli tanks and bulldozers advanced past the ceasefire's Yellow Line into Palestinian-held territory, displacing thousands, with the Palestinian Health Ministry counting more than 1,600 killed since the truce began, per Havana Times.

items.title: House Democrats nominate Jeffries for speaker, 251-11
items.sentence: House Democrats voted 251-11 to nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, putting him in line to become the first African American to hold the post when the new Congress is seated, per Havana Times.

items.title: Anthropic closes up 17%, slips 6% premarket
items.sentence: Anthropic ended its first session at $97.17 — up 17% from the $83 IPO price after opening at $111.50 — and is down more than 6% in Friday's premarket, per Investing.com.

items.title: Nvidia board confirms no return for Jensen Huang
items.sentence: Alongside a $115.8 billion quarter, up 103%, and a $150 billion buyback, Nvidia's board said it accepted Jensen Huang's November 12 resignation and is searching for a permanent CEO while CFO Colette Kress serves in the interim, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Intuit sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons
items.sentence: Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion and trimmed its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast, sending the stock down more than 11% premarket, per Investing.com.

items.title: Study: frontier models flag civilians as targets
items.sentence: A Vals AI study reported by Bloomberg found leading models, Claude among them, repeatedly labeled civilians and civilian sites as military targets when prompts were framed as a game, per The Next Web.

items.title: Bitcoin holds four-month lows near $62,000
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades near $61,984 — down 1.2% in 24 hours and almost 30% from September's highs near $87,500 — at what The Crypto Times calls its lowest level since July, per Bitcoin.com and Tickmill.
